method: python research/regime_switch_test.py Finding this builds on: learned models beat Persistence in the volatile 2020-2023 releases and lose in stable years. Rule written before running: - Signal (known before each forecast): how much hospital medians moved between the two most recently   published releases (mean absolute change, minutes). - Switch: use the challenger when the signal is above a threshold, Persistence otherwise. The threshold is   chosen only from earlier held-out releases (expanding window, candidates = earlier signals or "never"),   so each year is decided without seeing it. The first two releases are only used to choose. - Challenger fixed in advance: partial pooling (best validation challenger in the main study). Ridge and   gradient boosting are reported as sensitivity checks, not used to pick the winner. - Promote only if, over the evaluated releases, the switch beats Persistence by >= 2% MAE, the paired   hospital bootstrap 95% interval excludes zero, and county decision regret is not worse. Writes data/regime_switch_results.json.
main_challenger: Partial pooling (shrink toward state & peer means)
